categories.name: Initial visual impression
categories.note: QSimCity now opens on a daylight coastal city with a connected street grid, varied massing, harbor cranes, and farmland fringe; the reference retains denser interiors. QSimCity is interactive in about a second versus roughly a minute of staged loading.

categories.name: Skyline originality
categories.note: Entirely procedural geometry and textures with no third-party assets; the downtown cluster, refinery columns, cranes, and hilltop dome give each district a distinct silhouette.

categories.name: District differentiation
categories.note: Twelve districts built from distinct architectural kits on real blocks (wharf sheds, sawtooth halls, tank farms, podium towers, data halls); the reference uses roughly eight larger zones with denser interiors.

categories.name: Long-distance readability
categories.note: The whole pipeline reads in one frame; architecture carries district identity with labels as reinforcement, hidden entirely at street level.

categories.name: Medium-distance data-flow clarity
categories.note: Geography is the pipeline: the Processing Boulevard physically connects the stages west to east, and the convoy, banners, couriers, and container stacks make the flow visible mid-run.

categories.name: First-person detail
categories.note: Lane markings, crosswalks, lamps, street trees, parked cars, console kiosks, and three furnished enterable interiors at 1.7 m eye height; the reference still has more incidental street clutter.

categories.name: Orbit camera
categories.note: Damped drag-rotate and wheel zoom, clamped to the city bounds.

categories.name: Top-down camera
categories.note: Plan view showing the whole pipeline layout and street network.

categories.name: Fly camera
categories.note: Altitude control with bounds clamping and touch lift buttons.

categories.name: Walking camera
categories.note: Eye height 1.7 m with AABB and doorway collision; entering walk mode snaps to the nearest driving lane facing along the road, so the walker always starts in a street with a clear view.

categories.name: Day mode
categories.note: Sun shadows, sky dome with clouds, coastal water with sky reflection, and a fog-closed horizon; parity with the reference terrain, which keeps an edge in interior density.

categories.name: Night mode
categories.note: Hash-varied lit windows, street lamps with light pools, vehicle headlights, stars, and district glow; the reference night mode is a dimmer variant of its day scene.

categories.name: Touch and mobile presentation
categories.note: Touch orbit/pinch, an on-screen movement pad for walk and fly, and a touch-only mission path verified in the automated mobile profile; the reference documents emulation-only testing.

categories.name: Inspector integration
categories.note: Selection shows role, live state, provenance, certainty, and jump-to-timeline actions; the City Legend classifies every animated entity.

categories.name: Semantic animation
categories.note: Convoy, couriers, logical banners, container stacks, weather, and stage set pieces all derive from the trace; ambient life is explicitly ILLUSTRATIVE and no amplitude is animated as cargo.

categories.name: Loading presentation
categories.note: QSimCity reaches an interactive city in about a second; the reference displayed a sequence of loading captions for roughly a minute before the city appeared.

categories.name: Visual accessibility
categories.note: A complete non-WebGL mode including missions and the builder, axe-clean WCAG 2.2 AA, and never colour alone; the reference requires WebGL2.

categories.name: Overall polish
categories.note: Consistent design system, clean console across four browsers, no overlapping controls after the adversarial art-direction pass.

reference.state: live deployment of its main branch, 220 commits
